|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### paces.pose.DFLT_DEVICE *= 'cpu'*

onnxruntime execution device. “cpu” is the portable answer and the only one
CI would ever have; “cuda”/”mps” are a caller’s choice, not a default.

### paces.pose.DFLT_KEYPOINT_CONFIDENCE *= 0.3*

A keypoint below this score is noise, not evidence, and never widens a box.
This threshold is load-bearing, not decorative: rtmlib’s `Body` is a
top-down pipeline, so it returns a full 17-keypoint person for a frame with
nobody in it at all. Measured on a blank frame (rtmlib 0.0.15, balanced):
one “person”, every score ~0.11-0.13. Without this filter the locator would
hand the core a confident box around nothing, every time.

### paces.pose.DFLT_MIN_KEYPOINTS *= 4*

Fewer confident keypoints than this is not a person — it is a hallucinated
limb or two, and boxing it would hand the core a region with no subject in
it. The second half of the same defence: a real detection clears 0.3 on far
more than four joints, while the blank-frame phantom above clears it on none.

### paces.pose.DFLT_MODE *= 'balanced'*

“lightweight” | “balanced” | “performance”.

* **Type:**
  rtmlib `Body` accuracy/latency trade-off

### paces.pose.DFLT_PROBE_FPS *= 5.0*

Probe rate across an excerpt window, in samples per second — the POC’s rate.
Excerpts are 2.5–6 s loops, so ~5 fps is 13–30 looks: enough for the 4/96
envelope to shrug off a stray frame, cheap enough to run on CPU.

### paces.pose.POSE_EXTRA *= 'pose'*

The extra that carries this locator, and the stem of its recorded identity.

### *class* paces.pose.RtmlibPoseLocator(, probe_fps=5.0, mode='balanced', device='cpu', keypoint_confidence=0.3, min_keypoints=4, pose_estimator=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The pointable `subject_locator`: rtmlib pose boxes over a probed window.

Callable per the ADR-0005 §3 contract — a [`LocateQuery`](_autosummary/paces.derivation.html.md#paces.derivation.LocateQuery)
in, a [`SubjectObservation`](_autosummary/paces.derivation.html.md#paces.derivation.SubjectObservation) out, or `None`, the
honest “no crop”, when the window showed nobody. It never resolves a box:
that is the core’s [`resolve_crop_box()`](_autosummary/paces.derivation.html.md#paces.derivation.resolve_crop_box).

`pose_estimator` is the seam inside the seam: any
`callable(frame) -> (keypoints, scores)`. The default is rtmlib’s `Body`
(YOLOX + RTMPose, COCO-17); the replacements are already pointable —
rtmlib’s `Wholebody`, `Hand` and `Animal` solutions have exactly this
shape, and the ADR’s “hands + workpiece for cooking” case is one of them.
Tests inject a fake through it, which is how the contract is exercised with
no weights downloaded and no network reached.

All fields are keyword-only, and the defaults are the shipped policy.

#### *property* locator_name *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The policy identity the crop recipe records — **every** input that
can move a box, not just the model version.

`derive` reuses a stored box when this name and the core’s params
still match (ADR-0005 §3), so anything left out of it silently reuses a
box that something else measured. That is the whole point of the
fingerprint, so the probe rate and both keypoint thresholds are in it
alongside the model:

```default
rtmlib-pose@0.0.16;mode=balanced;fps=5;conf=0.3;minkp=4
```

An injected `pose_estimator` names *itself* — claiming rtmlib’s
version for a box rtmlib did not measure would be exactly the false
identity this exists to prevent — and drops `mode`, which is a
`Body` argument and means nothing to another estimator:

```default
rtmlib-pose@custom:mypkg.my_estimator;fps=5;conf=0.3;minkp=4
```

`device` is deliberately absent: it selects an execution provider,
not a policy, and putting it in would re-locate every box on a machine
change — a false honesty flag, which this codebase treats as the
failure mode it is.

### paces.pose.TEST_MODELS_ENVVAR *= 'PACES_TEST_MODELS'*

Opt-in for the real-model smoke test. Unset (CI, always) = no weights, no
inference — the contract is covered by fake locators instead.

### paces.pose.check_pose_requirements()

Preflight for the `[pose]` extra, per channel and never silently.

- `rtmlib` / `onnxruntime` — the locator and its inference backend.
- `cv2_providers` — rtmlib declares BOTH `opencv-python` and
  `opencv-contrib-python`, while the fleet standardises on the contrib
  superset (mixing’s single cv2 provider). An install can therefore end up
  with two distributions owning one `cv2` package. Reported, not fatal:
  it works until one of them is uninstalled, and a reader deserves to know
  — and, since neither package’s uninstall is safe once both are present
  (each claims files the other also claims), the note names the repair
  command rather than only the collision. See README’s “Auto-crop” section
  for the install recipe that avoids the pair in the first place
  (issue #20).

Downloads nothing: weights arrive on first inference, not on this check.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.pose.person_boxes(keypoints, scores, , frame_size, keypoint_confidence=0.3, min_keypoints=4)

One box per person, spanning that person’s *confident* keypoints.

`keypoints` is `(n_persons, n_keypoints, 2)` and `scores` is
`(n_persons, n_keypoints)` — rtmlib’s output shape, read here as plain
nested sequences, so this stays a pure function and numpy remains the
extra’s business rather than this module’s. A person carrying fewer than
`min_keypoints` confident points is dropped rather than boxed from noise;
boxes are clamped into the frame, and a degenerate one is dropped too.
Zero detections is `()` — evidence that nobody was there, not an error.

Order is rtmlib’s and means nothing: the seam is a *set* of regions per
instant (the core unions them), so no person-identity claim is made here.

```pycon
>>> person_boxes(
...     [[(10, 20), (30, 60)]], [(0.9, 0.9)],
...     frame_size=(100, 100), min_keypoints=2,
... )
((10, 20, 20, 40),)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

### paces.pose.probe_times(start_s, end_s, , probe_fps=5.0)

The instants to look at: ~\`\`probe_fps\`\` samples spread inside the window.

Samples sit at the midpoints of `n` equal slices, so each one is strictly
inside `[start_s, end_s)` — a probe on the closing edge would read the
next shot — and a window shorter than one probe interval still gets exactly
one look, at its middle.

```pycon
>>> tuple(round(t, 3) for t in probe_times(0.0, 1.0, probe_fps=5.0))
(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)
>>> tuple(round(t, 3) for t in probe_times(10.0, 10.05))
(10.025,)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

### paces.pose.rtmlib_pose *= RtmlibPoseLocator(probe_fps=5.0, mode='balanced', device='cpu', keypoint_confidence=0.3, min_keypoints=4, pose_estimator=None)*

no configuration, and the target a CLI
`--subject-locator paces.pose:rtmlib_pose` reference resolves to.

* **Type:**
  The ready-made locator
* **Return type:**
  [*SubjectObservation*](_autosummary/paces.html.md#paces.SubjectObservation) | *None*


# _autosummary/paces.projection.html.md

# paces.projection

The projection from analysis result to document: `to_document`.

A `Segmentation` is the *analysis result*; a
[`StepDocument`](_autosummary/paces.model.html.md#paces.model.StepDocument) is the *artifact* — committed, hand-edited,
rendered. Keeping them separate (one function between) is what lets the
segmenter re-run without touching hand-edited captions
(`docs/alignment/07 §9.1` decision 6).

### Module Attributes

| [`DECIMAL_PLACES`](_autosummary/paces.projection.html.md#paces.projection.DECIMAL_PLACES)   | Decimal places kept when converting computed seconds to wire decimals — matches the POC's 0.1 s working resolution with headroom.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`to_document`](_autosummary/paces.projection.html.md#paces.projection.to_document)(seg, \*[, doc_id, title, source, ...])   | Project a segmentation into a fresh step document.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

### paces.projection.DECIMAL_PLACES *= 3*

Decimal places kept when converting computed seconds to wire decimals —
matches the POC’s 0.1 s working resolution with headroom.

### paces.projection.to_document(seg, , doc_id='guide', title='', source=None, domain='generic', lang='en')

Project a segmentation into a fresh step document.

*source* is the media the spans refer into: a URI string, a
[`Source`](_autosummary/paces.model.html.md#paces.model.Source), or a mapping. Hand edits belong on the
returned document, never back on the segmentation.

* **Return type:**
  [`StepDocument`](_autosummary/paces.model.html.md#paces.model.StepDocument)


# _autosummary/paces.render.html.md

# paces.render

Render a [`StepDocument`](_autosummary/paces.model.html.md#paces.model.StepDocument) into learning material.

The renderer depends on the document and [`resolve()`](_autosummary/paces.model.html.md#paces.model.resolve) — never
on the analyser. v1 ships one renderer: a self-contained HTML practice page
(steps, counts, captions, deep links into the sources, and — when the document
has a metric grid — a count-along transport that paces you through the
routine, which is the behaviour the package is named after).

### Module Attributes

| [`ROLE_LABELS`](_autosummary/paces.render.html.md#paces.render.ROLE_LABELS)   | Span roles shown as deep links, in display order.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`render_html`](_autosummary/paces.render.html.md#paces.render.render_html)(doc)   | The practice page: steps, counts, deep links, captions, and (with a grid) the count-along transport.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### paces.render.ROLE_LABELS *= {'closeup': 'close-up', 'instruction': 'breakdown', 'performance': 'run-through'}*

Span roles shown as deep links, in display order.

### paces.render.render_html(doc)

The practice page: steps, counts, deep links, captions, and (with a
grid) the count-along transport. Self-contained; media-free by design —
derived clips arrive via `ArtifactRef` when the media layer exists.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md

# paces.segmenters

Segmentation is a seam, not a stage (ADR-0003).

`segment(media, ...)` takes media plus a `segmenter=`, and the segmenter
is where the variation lives. Segmenters are *registered* capabilities —
adding one is a new file with one `register(Capability(...))` call; nothing
existing is edited. The default is selected from what is present (the facts),
reported in `Segmentation.method`, and overridable by the one keyword.

A segmenter’s information can be intrinsic (features of the media), external
explicit (coordinates handed over), external derived (computed from the
surrounding annotations), or mixed — mixed being the normal case. v1 ships the
two maximally different ones so the seam is shaped by both rather than by one:

- `grid-placed` (external, derived — the que-calor shape): an ordered step
  list with domain durations, placed on the timeline by a metric grid.
- `explicit` (external, explicit — “ask the user”, first-class): boundaries
  or spans supplied directly, named when names were supplied, honestly unnamed
  when not.

Plus `chapters` (external, explicit): author-supplied chapter metadata — a
yt-dlp info dict or ffprobe’s `-show_chapters` output — is a complete named
segmentation for ~0 cost, and most tutorial content on the web carries it.

Honesty rules (`docs/alignment/07 §9.5`): a segmenter may never return a
step count it has no evidence for. Four legitimate return states — confident /
found-unnamed / proposed-uncertain / refused — all expressed by the type, none
by an exception.

### Functions

| [`capabilities`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.capabilities)()                          | The registered capability catalog (read-only view).            |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`register`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.register)(capability)                    | Register a segmentation capability; returns it for assignment. |
| [`segment`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.segment)([media, segmenter, steps, ...]) | Cut *media* into named steps, using whatever else is present.  |

### Classes

| [`Capability`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.Capability)(\*, name, gives, summary, target)     | What one method needs, gives, and costs.             |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SegStep`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.SegStep)(\*, id[, name, spans, confidence, ...])  | One named piece of the media, as an analysis result. |
| [`Segmentation`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.Segmentation)(\*[, steps, boundaries, unit, ...]) | What every segmenter returns.                        |

### *class* paces.segmenters.Capability(, name, gives, summary, target, needs=frozenset({}), reads=frozenset({}), boosts=dict(), requires=(), licence='MIT', base=0.0, s_per_min=0.0, usd_per_hour=0.0, device='cpu', fixed_s=0.0, resolution_s=1.0, calibrated_on=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What one method needs, gives, and costs. Selection reads ONLY this.

The record from `docs/alignment/06 §1.2`, reused unchanged so the
eventual planner and the segmenter registry share one declaration format.
`target` is a lazy `"module:func"` ref — listing a heavy capability
must not import its dependencies.

### *class* paces.segmenters.SegStep(, id, name='', spans=(), confidence=0.0, children=(), source='', evidence=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One named piece of the media, as an analysis result.

`name=''` means “found, not named” — a VALID state, not an error.
`spans` is a tuple because a step legitimately appears in several places
(run-through AND breakdown).

### *class* paces.segmenters.Segmentation(, steps=(), boundaries=(), unit='seconds', grid=None, confidence=0.0, method='', flags=(), elapsed_s=0.0, spent_usd=0.0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What every segmenter returns. Reviewable, re-runnable, arguable.

`boundaries` is separate from `steps` and populated even when naming
failed: nine excellent unnamed cuts are a useful, honest result. `steps`
may be empty while `boundaries` is not.

### paces.segmenters.capabilities()

The registered capability catalog (read-only view).

* **Return type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Capability`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.Capability)]

### paces.segmenters.register(capability)

Register a segmentation capability; returns it for assignment.

* **Return type:**
  [`Capability`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.Capability)

### paces.segmenters.segment(media=None, , segmenter=None, steps=None, boundaries=None, grid=None, metadata=None, k=None, catalog=None)

Cut *media* into named steps, using whatever else is present.

Returns a [`Segmentation`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.Segmentation) ALWAYS. A segmenter that cannot name the
steps returns `boundaries` and `steps=()`; when nothing applies the
result is the refused state (`flags=('no-signal', 'try: ...')`), not an
exception.

The seam: `segmenter=None` selects from what is present; a name pins it.

```pycon
>>> seg = segment(boundaries=[0, 10, 20], steps=['intro', 'verse'])
>>> [(s.name, s.spans) for s in seg.steps]
[('intro', ((0.0, 10.0),)), ('verse', ((10.0, 20.0),))]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Segmentation`](_autosummary/paces.segmenters.html.md#paces.segmenters.Segmentation)


# _autosummary/paces.tools.html.md

# paces.tools

Agent-callable tool surface over `paces` — plain functions with JSON-able
arguments returning JSON-ready values, deliberately CLI/MCP/HTTP-agnostic.

This module is the SSOT for “what paces can do”: every surface (the `cw`
CLI in `__main__.py` today; `py2mcp`/`qh` wrappers tomorrow) dispatches
over `_dispatch_funcs` and nothing else. Arguments that carry structure
(steps, grids, documents) accept a Python object, a JSON string, or a path to
a JSON file, so the same function serves the library, the shell, and an agent.

### Functions

| [`derive`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.derive)(document, \*, media[, output, ...])         | Derive real media (clip + gif + poster) for every excerpt-bearing span and write the refs into the document.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`edit`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.edit)(document, edits, \*, by[, reason, output])    | Apply typed patches to a document; every edit writes a Lock.                                                   |
| [`list_segmenters`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.list_segmenters)()                                  | The registered segmentation capabilities: name → what it needs/gives.                                          |
| [`measure_grid`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.measure_grid)(media, \*[, unit, subdivisions, ...]) | Measure a metric grid (tempo, macro-structure, estimated origin) from a local media file.                      |
| [`merge`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.merge)(committed, fresh, \*[, output])              | Merge a fresh analysis projection against the committed document.                                              |
| [`render`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.render)(document, \*[, output, renderer])           | Render a step document into learning material.                                                                 |
| [`resolve`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.resolve)(document)                                  | Compute absolute offsets and wall-clock times for a document's steps.                                          |
| [`segment`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.segment)([media, steps, boundaries, grid, ...])     | Cut media into steps using whatever else is present (ADR-0003).                                                |
| [`suggest_excerpts`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.suggest_excerpts)(document, \*[, units, role, ...]) | Mark each step's loopable sub-window (the `excerpt` derive cuts).                                              |
| [`to_document`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.to_document)(segmentation, \*[, doc_id, ...])       | Project a segmentation into a step document (the committed artifact).                                          |
| [`validate`](_autosummary/paces.tools.html.md#paces.tools.validate)(document)                                 | Schema + semantic check of a step document; returns `{"issues": [...]}`.                                       |

### paces.tools.derive(document, , media, output=None, subject_locator=None, roles='clip,gif,poster', aspect=None, pad=None)

Derive real media (clip + gif + poster) for every excerpt-bearing
span and write the refs into the document. Needs the [media] extra.

`document` must be a *path* here (the anchor for the `media/` dir
and the crop-recipes sidecar — ADR-0005 §1); library callers with an
in-memory document use [`paces.derivation.derive_document()`](_autosummary/paces.derivation.html.md#paces.derivation.derive_document) with an
explicit store. `media` is one local file, or `{"<source-id>":
"<path>"}` when several sources carry excerpts. `subject_locator` is
a lazy `"module:attr"` ref to an ADR-0005 §3 locator; the default is
no crop, and `paces.pose:rtmlib_pose` is the shipped pointable one
(rtmlib pose boxes, `pip install paces[pose]`). The updated document is written back to `output` (default:
the document path itself — derive’s media side effects and the refs
pointing at them must not go out of sync); the returned payload carries
`flags` — read them, they are the honesty report.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.edit(document, edits, , by, reason=None, output=None)

Apply typed patches to a document; every edit writes a Lock.

`edits` is a list of `{"op": "set", "path": "/steps/b4/name",
"value": ...}` (JSON value, string, or file path). `by` identifies the
editor (“user:thor”, “agent:<model>”). Locked paths survive
regeneration (see `merge`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.list_segmenters()

The registered segmentation capabilities: name → what it needs/gives.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.measure_grid(media, , unit='eight', subdivisions=8, total_units=None, output=None)

Measure a metric grid (tempo, macro-structure, estimated origin) from
a local media file. Needs the [audio] extra.

Returns `{"grid", "confidence", "flags", "evidence"}` — origin is an
estimate (first beat of the music region) and the flags say so; override
with an explicit `grid=` on `segment` when it is wrong.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.merge(committed, fresh, , output=None)

Merge a fresh analysis projection against the committed document.

Locked paths keep the committed value; everything else takes the fresh
value; protected committed-only steps survive. This is how re-running
analysis never eats a hand edit.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.render(document, , output=None, renderer='html')

Render a step document into learning material.

`renderer='html'` (v1’s one implementation) produces the self-contained
practice page. Returns the output path when `output=` is given,
otherwise the rendered text itself.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### paces.tools.resolve(document)

Compute absolute offsets and wall-clock times for a document’s steps.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.segment(media=None, , steps=None, boundaries=None, grid=None, metadata=None, segmenter=None, k=None, output=None)

Cut media into steps using whatever else is present (ADR-0003).

`steps`, `boundaries`, `grid` and `metadata` accept JSON values,
JSON strings, or paths to JSON files — `metadata` notably takes a
yt-dlp `.info.json` (its `chapters` become a named segmentation).
Returns the segmentation as a JSON-ready dict (also written to
`output=` when given) — honest about naming
(`flags: ['naming-abstained']`) and about refusal
(`flags: ['no-signal', 'try: ...']`); never a fabricated step list.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.suggest_excerpts(document, , units=None, role='performance', overwrite=False, output=None)

Mark each step’s loopable sub-window (the `excerpt` derive cuts).

v1 heuristic (issue #3): the excerpt is the span’s whole grid window;
`units=N` takes the first N metric units instead. Never overwrites an
existing excerpt unless `overwrite` (and never a locked one). Returns
`{"document", "flags", "suggested"}`; writes to `output=` when given.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.to_document(segmentation, , doc_id='guide', title='', source=None, domain='generic', lang='en', output=None)

Project a segmentation into a step document (the committed artifact).

`source` is the media URI the spans refer into. With `output=`, the
canonical wire form is also written to that path.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### paces.tools.validate(document)

Schema + semantic check of a step document; returns `{"issues": [...]}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# For AI agents

`paces` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/paces/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/paces/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`paces.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/paces/paces.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/paces/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
